chunks: With this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who recites the Surah of Al-Hujurat every night or every day will be among the visitors of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.زُوَّارِ: Visitors (plural of zahir/zawwar), implying spiritual proximity or honor
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْحُجُرَاتِ: Surah Al-Hujurat (The Chambers), the 49th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ ص: Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Hujurat daily?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith establishes a tangible spiritual reward for the consistent recitation of Surah Al-Hujurat, linking the act of Quranic devotion directly to the honor of being among the Prophet’s *Zawwar* (visitors) in the afterlife. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the intercessory status of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet, where regular engagement with the Quran serves as a means of cultivating closeness to them. The term 'visitors' implies a special, intimate connection to the Prophet’s spiritual presence, elevating the reciter’s status beyond mere obedience to divine command.
